changes.before: the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 2 to 2-1/4 percent
changes.after: the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-3/4 to 2 percent

changes.before: Although growth of household spending has picked up from earlier in the year, growth of business fixed investment has been soft.
changes.after: Although household spending has been rising at a strong pace, business fixed investment and exports have weakened.

changes.before: The Committee will conclude the reduction of its aggregate securities holdings in the System Open Market Account in August, two months earlier than previously indicated.
Voting against the action were Esther L. George and Eric S. Rosengren, who preferred at this meeting to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent.
changes.after: Voting against the action were James Bullard, who preferred at this meeting to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent; and Esther L. George and Eric S. Rosengren, who preferred to maintain the target range at 2 percent to 2-1/4 percent.

parsed.rationale: The Committee delivered a second 25bp cut and described weakening investment and exports, with a new dissent favoring a larger cut, though forward guidance was unchanged and hawkish dissents persisted. The shift is a moderate dovish continuation rather than a change in direction.

spans.quote: the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 2 to 2-1/4 percent
Although growth of household spending has picked up from earlier in the year, growth of business fixed investment has been soft.
The Committee will conclude the reduction of its aggregate securities holdings in the System Open Market Account in August, two months earlier than previously indicated.
Voting against the action were Esther L. George and Eric S. Rosengren, who preferred at this meeting to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent.
the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-3/4 to 2 percent
Although household spending has been rising at a strong pace, business fixed investment and exports have weakened.

Voting against the action were James Bullard, who preferred at this meeting to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent; and Esther L. George and Eric S. Rosengren, who preferred to maintain the target range at 2 percent to 2-1/4 percent.
